title: Take a story end-to-end with another role
why_matters: Most of what BAs do happens in seams — between product and engineering, between business and ops, between design and dev. Walking a single story from one side of a seam to the other, with whoever owns the other side, is how you stop being a hand-off node and start being someone who can stitch.
steps: Pick one story in the backlog that you don't currently own. Choose one where the other owner is from a discipline you've engaged with less (designer, ops, QA).
Ask if you can shadow them through their portion of the work — not just the meetings, the actual work.
Take notes specifically on what they decide that you wouldn't have thought to decide.
Send them a thank-you note with one concrete observation. "I hadn't appreciated that you check X before Y" beats "thanks for your time".
success_criteria: You have shadowed a complete piece of work from another discipline. Notes exist on three decisions they made that you wouldn't have. The other person has received a specific thank-you.
reflection_prompt: What surprised you most about how their decisions are made, and what would you do differently in your own work because of it?
